text:
Morgan: Quick sync on follow-ups from the recent postmortems (missing spans + bad aggregation + ETL lag). I think we're seeing a recurring pattern across three incidents in the last 60d.
Nina: ack. I started a short root-cause notes doc earlier, will paste link in a sec.
Arjun: can you summarize the pattern? is this infra timing or parser-related?
Morgan: pattern = intermittent span drop at the ingest hop + late batch window that triggers an aggregate rewrite. Not always correlated with host OOMs.
Lee: saw similar in 02/2026 where partial consumer restart caused duplicate checkpoint state, which then reprocessed partial windows.
Nina: my preliminary read: two things - (1) our span-ingest service drops spans if consumer backlog > 1M (we truncate unacked messages), (2) ETL windowing assumes idempotent replays but aggregation job isn't fully idempotent for out-of-order late arrivals.
Sylvia: that explains the drift in the hourly rollups we saw.
Kevin: timeline proposal: triage -> quick mitigations -> rollout fix -> validate with canary dataset. ETA?
Morgan: propose owners and due dates: 
  - Mitigation (stop truncation): Arjun - 2026-03-30
  - Aggregation idempotency patch: Nina - 2026-04-07
  - ETL consumer backpressure config + dashboards: Lee - 2026-03-28
  - Canary validation & sample repro: Sylvia - 2026-04-09
Arjun: I can take mitigation. Quick plan: bump retention of consumer queue to avoid truncation and add an alert if unacked > 500k.
Morgan: please add alert as metric and create runbook step to fail-safe to retry instead of truncate.
Arjun: putting PR for retention now. will add alert rule and link.
incidents-bot: New alert rule created: consumer_unacked_count > 500000 for 5m (owner: Arjun). Incident link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-213
Nina: for aggregation patch I'll add idempotency key on the rollup writer and run local replay tests. planning a canary for 100 orgs.
Lee: ETL backpressure: change consumer max inflight to 200 and enable compaction windowing. quick config change -> low risk.
Sylvia: for validation I'll prepare a canned dataset with three scenarios: normal, late-arrival bursts, partial replay. will run nightly for 7 days post-rollout.
Kevin: can we get an explicit owner for post-deploy verification? who's stepping?
Nina: I'll own verification of correctness metrics (rollup delta < 0.1%). Sylvia will run replay tests and provide sample dashboards.
Morgan: good. please update the postmortem action tracker (https://redwood.atlassian.com/pm/PM-2026) with items and link PRs. we'll review next Wed 2026-04-01 10:00 PT.
Lee: adding runbook note: if aggregation drift > 0.5% for > 2 hours, rollback to last good rollup snapshot and notify on-call.
Kevin: add cost impact note too — large replays spike egress and compute. include estimated RIs.
Arjun: PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/412 — retention bump + alert.
Nina: PR for rollup idempotency coming later today.
Sylvia: created test datasets and placed in s3://redwood-test/replay/pm-2026.
Morgan: thanks. A few small asks before we close this thread: (1) owners add explicit verification steps and expected metrics, (2) set verification due dates, (3) add rollback procedure into the runbook.
Kevin: I'll schedule a short 30m follow-up on 2026-04-01 after the review to validate runbook and SLO impacts.
Morgan: perfect. I'll mark this thread as action-tracker-updated once the (a) PRs are linked and (b) Jira updated. tagging everyone: @Nina @Arjun @Lee @Sylvia @Kevin :thumbsup:
Nina: :thumbsup: will update PM-2026 tasks now.
Arjun: taking ownership of mitigation, will notify when staged.
incidents-bot: Reminder set: postmortem-review PM-2026 on 2026-04-01 10:00 PT (attendees: Morgan, Nina, Arjun, Lee, Sylvia, Kevin).
Morgan: closing for now — short checkin after PR reviews. thanks all.
